scenarios.theme: Redis rejects writes even though an eviction policy is configured. Why?
scenarios.assumptions: The instance uses a volatile policy, but almost every key has no expiry. Memory-growing writes now fail. What will you investigate?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Redis rejects writes even though an eviction policy is configured. Why?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Check maxmemory, actual policy and eviction eligibility, inspect keys/TTLs and memory overhead, then choose a policy appropriate to the role

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: An allkeys policy may restore cache admission but can remove any eligible cached item; noeviction preserves keys at the cost of write failure

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Raising memory without understanding growth/eligibility only postpones the problem.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to evict, expire; interview frequency is not claimed.

scenarios.assumptions: A massive catalog aggregate is read repeatedly from one key and dominates network/CPU. What will you choose?

scenarios.theme: Eviction removes business records mixed with product copies. What is the architecture decision?
scenarios.assumptions: A shared Redis instance uses allkeys eviction for product caching and also holds the only accepted background work records. What will you do?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Eviction removes business records mixed with product copies. What is the architecture decision?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Separate rebuildable cache admission from authoritative work durability, with explicit storage, retention and recovery for accepted jobs

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Separate stores/instances cost operations; a carefully engineered common system can work only if its guarantees satisfy both roles

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Turning off eviction can replace data loss with admission failure, which the service must still handle honestly.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to evict, persist; interview frequency is not claimed.
